LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. away.blurb: Seahawks injury update: Jadarian Price return timeline sounds promising - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Hurts reportedly out for season Seahawks injury update: Jadarian Price return timeline sounds promising The Seattle Seahawks need running back help in the worst way. It'll be at least two weeks until Jadarian Price is eligible to return from injured reserve, while Zach Charbonnet has a chance to play against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7. Mike Macdonald revealed a little bit of a timeline as far as Price's return during his Friday morning show with Brock and Salk on Seattle Sports 710 . "He's doing great," Macdonald said. "We should be looking at a sooner rather than later return after this [Kansas City Chiefs] game." Price has been out since the start of Week 4 with a chest injury, which he aggravated in practice after getting the initial injury in Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals. The rookie out of Notre Dame has had a couple of costly fumbles , but since George Holani and Emanuel Wilson have also since lost a combined three fumbles, he's hardly the only culprit. Price has offered some explosiveness in the run game in a limited sample size, and his speed is what the main running back room lacks. Mookie Alexander Sat, October 17, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Mike Macdonald had no update on Charbonnet's progress (or, maybe, no update he was willing to share), but it's worth noting that Charbonnet must be activated this upcoming week or else he reverts to injured reserve for the rest of the season. Seattle opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 1, prior to the Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Once that window expires, the Seahawks either have to place him on the 53-man roster or end his season. The latter is obviously not happening unless there's some unbelievably worrying setback, so we're left to turn our attention to Price. In an ideal world, Charbonnet is back in Week 7 and Price is back in Week 8, at which point the running back room should be a lot stronger.

The Jags are playing their second consecutive international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense. Jaguars o-line vs. Texans defense: The Jags will be without left tackle Anton Harrison , who needs surgery. As Jaguars head coach Liam Coen noted this week, divisional games offer a chance for a different slate of circumstances compared to typical weeks. "Know that every time that you line up against this team, it's going to be a fight. It's going to be a brawl. That's what's great about football, that's what's great about rivalries, is that you have a level of respect for each other," Coen said. "Because you know any given Sunday, anything can happen, especially in rivalry-type games and understanding what you can learn from each of these opportunities that you play against one another in, and how well you start to get to know each other in ways in terms of what they want to do, what we want to do. I think this will be a close game because, on paper, these two teams are close in nearly every area. The Jaguars have a much better running game than the Texans do, but both teams have talented quarterbacks who are playing well, proven head coaches, explosive pass-catchers, strong defenses, so on and so forth. While the Texans are 1-4, everything indicates this is a closer matchup on paper than one would think just looking at the records. With that said, I think the fact the Jaguars have been a more complete team this season is no accident and is not owrth simply tossing aside. The Jaguars have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season, and the Jaguars have more things to hang their hat on right now than this Texans squad does. After two wins without Williams, the Bears got blown out 31-7 in Green Bay last week. The Falcons had won two straight games as well before falling 30-23 to the Ravens in Week 5. They, too, have had quarterback issues this season. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 6 matchup with a final score prediction. Bears vs. Falcons Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: We have a lot of early-week questions at quarterback for both teams. Caleb Williams has a chance to return for the Bears after a Week 2 injury, and Michael Penix Jr. may be out with a rib injury for the Falcons, forcing Atlanta to turn to Tua Tagovailoa. The Bears have only gone OVER the total once this season, when they put up 59 points themselves in Week 1. I think Williams’ return can help them to a high-scoring win in Atlanta. away.headline: Bears Friday injury report: Will Caleb Williams play vs. Falcons?

Quarterback Caleb Williams practiced in full for a third straight day, an indication that he's poised to return to the lineup in Week 6. away.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Oct 17 (Field Level Media) - Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3).

away.headline: Chicago Bears defeat Atlanta Falcons 31-23 as quarterback Caleb Williams returns from injury
away.blurb: Bears fans celebrate Williams' return, look ahead to Thursday night matchup ATLANTA -- Caleb Williams completed his first 12 passes in his return from a hamstring injury, D'Andre Swift ran for two touchdowns and the Chicago Bears beat the Atlanta Falcons 31-23 on Sunday. Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon, who was activated from the physically unable to perform list before the game in his return from a calf injury, had three sacks and two forced fumbles. Gordon's big day was capped by a sack of Michael Penix Jr. and forced fumble with 2:54 remaining and the Bears protecting a 31-23 lead. The fumble was recovered by Devin Bush at the Atlanta 28. The Bears ran out the clock inside the Atlanta 5. After missing three games, Williams was both mobile and accurate in his impressive return for the Bears (4-2). He opened the game by completing 6 of 6 passes for 64 yards, including a 14-yard scoring pass to Colston Loveland, on Chicago's opening drive. Williams was 12 of 12 for 142 yards before throwing his first incompletion in the second quarter. Though the Bears won two of three games with Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum filing in at quarterback, Williams' return sparked the offense. He completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards with one touchdown. Penix threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to Jahan Dotson in the second quarter. The perfectly placed back-shoulder fade pass cut the Bears' lead to 14-7, but a fumbled fair catch attempt by Zachariah Branch gave Chicago possession at the Atlanta 10 late in the first half. Branch also lost a fumble on a kickoff return late in the third quarter. Bears fans celebrate win, Williams' return, look ahead to Thursday "Caleb balled out," Hasler said. "Bears played great and yeah bears are back in town ready for Thursday." Fans are already looking ahead to Thursday's game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field, anticipating another lively atmosphere as the Bears return home. Bears: DB Cam Lewis was evaluated for a concussion in the second quarter. RB Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) was inactive. RG Jonah Jackson was ruled doubtful to return with a hip injury in the third quarter. Falcons: ILB Kendal Daniels was carted off the field midway through the third quarter after making a helmet-first tackle on tight end Colston Loveland. Daniels' head snapped back and Falcons players circled Daniels as he was strapped onto the stretcher and driven off the field. He was officially ruled out with a neck injury and the Falcons announced he was alert and had movement in all extremities and was being evaluated at Grady Hospital in Atlanta . ... ILB Divine Deablo (arm) was ruled out in the second quarter. CB Avieon Terrell (left shoulder) left the game in the second quarter. DB Billy Bowman Jr. was ruled doubtful with a hamstring injury. home.headline: Injury Update: Caleb Williams questionable for Sunday's game vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Injury Update: Caleb Williams questionable for Sunday's game vs. Falcons Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Jacob Funk/Chicago Bears Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was a full participant in practice Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons in Atlanta. "Confidence is a big part of it as well, but I know he wants to play. He's a competitor. It's been not fun for him the last few weeks watching from the sideline, just like any guy that loves football. It's been a tough deal for him. I know he's itching to get back out there and help us win ball games. If we feel really good as a front office, a coaching staff and player himself about playing, then we'll go ahead and go with it." Like Williams, cornerback Kyler Gordon was a full participant in practice all week and is questionable for Sunday's game. The Bears have until next week to activate Gordon from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, where he has been since before training camp began due to a calf injury. "He's done a great job taking everything that we've assigned him so far," Johnson said. "I do feel good about him [playing], whether that's this week or next week. I do feel good about him being able to contribute to this team and help us out, and there's a number of ways he can do that. But I'm encouraged with what I've seen so far." Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson is also questionable with a hip injury he sustained last weekend against the Packers that limited him in practice all week. Bears players who have been ruled out of Sunday's contest are running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo (quadriceps) and linebackers T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Keyshaun Elliott (quadriceps). "What showed up in his college tape was the violence with which he played," Johnson said. "He's got an aggressive demeanor about him. Despite the injuries that have held him back, training camp last year, ACL, all these things, hopeful that that part comes out. He's very similar to a lot of these guys that we're bringing in. They love football, and so being out there on the grass competing, that's really where they come to life the most. So, I'm excited to see him go out there and compete." news Injury Update: Bears RB Kyle Monangai ruled out, QB Caleb Williams questionable for Packers game Bears running back Kyle Monangai has been ruled out of Sunday's game in Green Bay with a toe injury, while quarterback Caleb Williams returned to practice Friday on a limited basis for the first time since hurting his hamstring Sept. 20 versus the Vikings. news Injury Update: Caleb Williams officially ruled out for Sunday's game vs. Jets news Injury Update: Bears rule out Caleb Williams, will start Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum vs. Eagles The Bears ruled Caleb Williams out of Monday night's game against the Eagles with a hamstring injury, but they have not yet announced whether Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum will replace him. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. DraftKings Sportsbook has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites, a full one-point change from where the spread was on Tuesday morning . Still, Jackson didn't practice on Wednesday, which makes his status for Sunday a little murky. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that the two-time league MVP is "day-to-day." Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. The Baltimore Ravens are no strangers to playing without their star quarterback, and that helps to explain why they're 3-point favorites on Sunday despite backup Tyler Huntley starting. Here are my NFL picks ahead of this Sunday, Oct. 18, clash, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET today. Ravens vs Browns prediction today: Ravens -3.5 The Baltimore Ravens are chasing their fourth straight win over the Cleveland Browns , and Lamar Jackson's absence isn't deterring me from fading a Cleveland team that crashed back to earth last weekend. Even with Todd Monken's knowledge of his former team, I'll lay the points - playable anywhere from -3 to -4. Tyler Huntley , one of the NFL's better backup QBs, led Baltimore to an overtime win in Week 5, and he's now 3-0 as a starter since last season. But this pick is more about what Derrick Henry can do against a Browns defense that's allowing 117.4 rushing yards per game and could be without Carson Schwesinger and Mason Graham (both questionable). On the other side of the ball, look for the visitors to be opportunistic against Deshaun Watson , who was sacked eight times in Week 5 and may have to do more in the passing game given the hosts' backfield injuries. The Ravens are 4-2 ATS in their past six road games , and two of the last three meetings between these teams have been emphatic Baltimore blowouts. TOP PICK Ravens vs Browns player prop: Derrick Henry Over 88.5 rushing yards The Ravens have handed Henry a heavy workload once again this season - he leads the league with 113 carries while averaging 95.2 YPG on the ground, and yet there's room for more with Jackson sidelined. This AFC North duel is a favorable matchup for King Henry, too, with the Browns giving up 134 rushing yards last weekend in New York and dealing with injuries across the defensive line . I don't see that banged-up unit being a match for Baltimore's powerhouse RB, who sits third in the NFL in yards after contact (262). Henry has gone past this O/U number in eight of his last 10 outings , and a run-heavy script should produce 20+ carries. Ravens vs Browns combo The Ravens have scored 24+ points in each of their wins this year , and this line feels too low despite Jackson being sidelined. The Over is 7-3 in Baltimore's last 10 games, and it's been a winning ticket in the past five meetings between these teams . With Cleveland sweating on the health of key defensive playmakers, Huntley can deliver a similar stat line to his SNF effort against the Falcons (201 passing yards, two TD passes, no turnovers), while the Browns' offense is boosted by KC Concepcion clearing the concussion protocol. When Baltimore isn't riding Henry and the ground game, look for Mark Andrews to be a key checkdown option for Huntley. Andrews has 22 catches through five contests, and he's finished with 6+ targets in four of those outings . Ravens moneyline Mark Andrews Over 3.5 receptions Ravens vs Browns touchdown scorer: Harold Fannin Jr. The Browns feel likelier to have success through the air than on the ground on Sunday, and Harold Fannin Jr. stands out as an anytime TD pick after grabbing three scores already this year . away.headline: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out
away.blurb: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Hurts reportedly out for season Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out While it had been established that the Ravens would likely be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for another game, he has officially been ruled out, along with three others. Center Cam Jurgens also remains out as he works his way back from concussion protocol. The Ravens traded for the former Philadelphia Eagles center before Week 5, but he was in the protocol when the trade took place. With Jurgens out, this means rookie guard Vega Ioane will step in as the center yet again. Additionally, guard Andrew Vorhees is questionable with a foot injury, and he may need more time to heal as well. Emery Jones Jr. may get the start on Sunday, especially so as not to lead to a further injury for Vorhees. The issue is that Jones is also questionable, pointing to what could be an issue if both are not able to play. Finally, defensive tackle Broderick Washington is out due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 5. Despite a full week of practice as a full participant, rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is also questionable. He may not be ready to play, as he is still being designated to return from IR. No other players have injury statuses for the game. Despite the laundry list of injuries reported, the Ravens will have most of their key players available. Two concerns arose on Thursday when wide receiver Zay Flowers appeared on the injury report with a toe ailment, and linebacker Mike Green joined him with a hamstring. Both were limited and were upgraded to full participants on Friday. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson is also making his return after undergoing a procedure to fix his broken finger. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke about the defender, saying he is excited to get him back out on the field. (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images) James Brizuela Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:20 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens are gearing up for their divisional matchup with their former offensive coordinator-turned-head coach, Todd Monken, and his Cleveland Browns. The full final injury report is as follows: Jackson is still dealing with his sprained ankle and will now miss his second consecutive game. Joining Jackson is rookie tight end Matt Hibner, who suffered a hand injury. Reports indicate that Hibner has a cast on his hand, pointing to what could be a significant injury. There are no other red flags unless Jones or Vorhees are both unable to play, which would put the Baltimore offensive line in a very tough spot.

Trey Hendrickson Will Make His Return "We're always going to try to have the best interest of the player," Minter said. "The path that we went down was really in [Hendrickson]'s best interest, both short-term and long-term. [I'm] excited for him to be back out there." The Ravens ruled out defensive tackle Broderick Washington Jr. (ankle), who didn't practice Thursday or Friday. He has six tackles so far this season. Minter also ruled out Cam Jurgens (concussion) for Sunday's game, meaning rookie Vega Ioane will get another start at center.. The Ravens also have other offensive line injuries to monitor with guards Andrew Vorhees (foot) and Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) both questionable to play. They were limited throughout the week. Wide receivers Zay Flowers (toe) and Rashod Bateman (shoulder) are good to go with no injury designation. Flowers was limited Thursday and Friday but Bateman returned to full participation. Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane could return from injured reserve after he suffered a wrist injury in Week 1 in Indianapolis. Lane had three full days of practice this week and is listed as questionable. He would have to be removed from injured reserve this weekend to play. While the Ravens could be at full strength at receiver, they're short at tight end with rookie Matt Hibner (hand) ruled out for Sunday's game. He didn't practice this week. Per Minter, the rookie tight end is not a candidate to be placed on injured reserve. Multiple Browns Leaders Return to Practice, Questionable to Play All three were limited in Friday's practice, along with veteran defensive end Derek Barnett (ankle). The Browns ruled out defensive tackle Mike Hall (ankle), quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back), defensive tackle Kalia Davis (quad), guard Teven Jenkins (back) and running back Dylan Sampson (knee). Jackson has yet to practice since suffering his ankle injury 12 days ago and will miss his second straight game. "It's day-by-day, I would say," Head Coach Jesse Minter. away.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
away.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Bleacher Report • 8h 🚨 Davante Out 6-10 Weeks Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. home.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Bleacher Report • 8h 🚨 Davante Out 6-10 Weeks Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the fifth straight week in a row now, we can say that the Tennessee Titans fell short of expectations. What was initially painted as a bounce-back campaign for Robert Saleh and the franchise has turned into a recurring question from fans in Nashville: "How much longer will it take for this thing to change?" The answer? I wish I could give it to you. Instead, the Tennessee Titans stand alongside the Miami Dolphins as one of the only two teams without a win this season. On the road against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6, it no longer appears to be about things changing in the present. At this point, any sign of life on the way to a victory would do. In the split spirit of both optimism and reality, here's one reason the Titans will beat the Colts tomorrow, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction to split the difference. Will: Robert Saleh's defense bounces back Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh walks onto the field during pre-game warmups against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a score on 26 completions. The QB also found a touchdown on the ground as Houston ran away with a 26-3 victory. If Tennessee wins this week, it will be by slowing down a hot Colts offense with a massive recovery. Shut down Jonathan Taylor in the backfield, and who knows how far this team can get. Positively, Tennessee has done a solid job stopping the run this year in large part. The Texans rushed for just 79 yards last week in total. With star WR Alec Pierce on IR and reserve Ashton Dulin also set to miss time, QB Daniel Jones' options will be relatively limited. A Titans win would be about finding spurts of offensive momentum by way of defensive playmaking. Won't: Cam Ward continues to decline The lack of that offensive momentum, however, is the exact reason why Tennessee could come up short. Second-year QB Cam Ward has failed to generate any real momentum under center this season, and his shortcomings have the Titans punching up to begin with. Against Houston, Ward took four sacks and threw an interception for the third straight game. He's thrown less than 200 yards in four of the Titans' five games (five losses) this season. His full total is now out to three scores and three interceptions. That simply won't cut it for Tennessee's needed franchise QB. Promising weapons surrounding Ward, such as Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate in the WR room, haven't been able to elevate his underwhelming run. If the Titans fall short, you can safely bet it will be due to Ward once again falling short of the bar. Prediction: Titans lose, 27-17 Much like the Titans' early-season loss to the Texans last season (in which Tennessee went scoreless), I expect a relative surge of momentum from the offense. However, I don't expect the Titans to find a road win as they did vs. the Cardinals in 2025. Indy, while coming off a loss to the Steelers, has already collected two wins and consistently scored 20+ points. Their lone contest failing that margin came against Houston, in a 19-17 victory. Daniel Jones passes twice as much as Cam Ward (hardly hyperbole), and Taylor remains one of the NFL's premier backs. I predict Tennessee will surpass their three-point showing from Week 5, and things may even appear interesting early on. Still, there's nothing of present about this Titans team to suggest that a breakthrough is on the horizon. In an AFC South-bound duel tomorrow, I unfortunately anticipate the losing streak to continue. All we can hope for is a surprise from Saleh and a squad that, up to now, haven't done near enough to spark midseason hope. Tennessee is coming off an embarrassing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans in Week 5, while Indianapolis fell on the road 34-22 to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Both teams will be eyeing major bounce-back victories, and with it being a division game, the stakes are a little higher than usual. With all that said, let's take a look at what the experts think about Sunday's AFC South battle between the Titans and the Colts. Titans vs. Colts Expert Game Picks CBS Sports: Colts 24, Titans 20 Words from the author Tyler Sullivan: You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket." Pro Football Talk: Colts 27, Titans 10 Words from the author Mike Florio: The Colts can’t afford to lose at home to a team that can’t do much on either side of the ball. Jeremy Bergman: Colts 24, Titans 19 Brooke Cersosimo: Colts 32, Titans 23 Gennaro Filice: Titans 14, Colts 13 Bobby Kownack: Colts 24, Titans 20 Dan Parr: Colts 27, Titans 20 Words from author Gennaro Filice: Admittedly, Tennessee has played like the most beatable team in the entire league, particularly on offense, where the Titans rank dead last in points and yards by comfortable margins. But Saleh’s D at least has some bite, especially up front. home.headline: Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts
home.blurb: The Colts are seeking consistency at linebacker, with snaps divided in Week 5 between Akeem Davis-Gaither (52 snaps), Austin Ajiake (32 snaps), CJ Allen (24 snaps) and Bryce Boettcher (11 snaps) with starting WILL linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) out. As with Davis-Gaither, the Colts see value in Pratt's experience not only in the NFL, but with Anarumo's system. Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts signed the 30-year-old Pratt, who started 12 games for them in 2025, to their practice squad on Tuesday. While Germaine Pratt went unsigned up until Tuesday, he found a way to still be involved in football. The 30-year-old veteran linebacker spent time in the summer as a volunteer coach at North Carolina State , where he worked with his alma mater's linebackers. He eventually had a tryout with the Dallas Cowboys, though he didn't sign. This week, Pratt got his chance to get back into playing instead of coaching. The Colts signed him to their practice squad on Tuesday, and while it's too early to tell if and when he'll make his 2026 debut, Pratt said his goal is to use his experience to bring leadership to the Colts' linebacker room. "Helping the defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know," Pratt said. "So help it stabilize and settle it down, make tackles, whatever the case may be, get some turnovers." Pratt has played all but four of his 112 NFL games for Lou Anarumo, his defensive coordinator with the Cincinnati Bengals (2019-2024) and Colts (2025). In 2025, Pratt signed with the Colts in October after being released by the Las Vegas Raiders and started 12 games, totaling 101 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception. The experienced WILL linebacker has had over 100 tackles with at least one interception and one forced fumble every year since 2023. "Just adding a veteran presence is big in there," head coach Shane Steichen said. "He's played a lot of football in this league, made a lot of plays, and any time you can add good players to your roster, you want to do that." In the immediate future, whether Pratt could factor into that group on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans – he'd have to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad – remains to be seen given he didn't participate in training camp and took the field for his first practice of the 2026 season on Wednesday. "I don't know the plan," Pratt said. The Saints have the league’s 20th-ranked offense (322.0 yards per game) and the 25th-ranked defense (361.0 yards per game) as they head into MetLife Stadium against a Giants team that has a chance to go 4-0 at home for the first time since 2008, when they got off to a 6-0 start at home. Despite the Saints’ struggles, they enter this game as a 1.5-point favorite per FanDuel , which is a head-scratcher considering they have averaged 21.3 points in their last three games, while the home team has averaged 25 points per game. But odds aside, the NFC East-leading Giants’ goal, according to head coach John Harbaugh, is simple: stack wins. “You always know what they are, but you know you’ve got to stack wins to make the December standings matter,” Harbaugh said when asked how much he pays attention to the standings at this point in the season. “So, we focus on the next game.” The Giants, according to Tankathon , have to make hay, so to speak. They face a remaining schedule with a combined winning percentage of .484, with their four toughest opponents being the 49ers, Jaguars, Lions, and Browns. All four of those challenging opponents land on the schedule after the Giants’ Week 8 bye. But to focus on what the Giants might do this week, let’s look at the best- and worst-case scenarios. Why the Giants Will Beat the Saints Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (29) runs the ball during the third quarter against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If there was ever a good week for the Giants’ rushing game to snap out of its funk, this would be it. The league’s 30th-ranked run defense has struggled big time this season, allowing 4.9 yards per rushing attempt. If there was ever a good week for the Giants’ rushing game to snap out of its funk, this would be it. The league’s 30th-ranked run defense has struggled big time this season, allowing 4.9 yards per rushing attempt. It also ranks last in the league in defensive rush success (52.5%), meaning it struggles to stop opponents from gaining the minimum required yardage on a run (excluding kneeldowns and scrambles). The Giants’ rushing offense has not been the same since quarterback Jaxson Dart landed on IR with a season-ending knee injury. Although it ranks 17th in total rushing yards, it also averages a dismal 3.7 yards per attempt, 24th in the league. As if the rushing game’s struggles aren’t enough, it will be interesting to see if Harbaugh decides to reduce running back Cam Skattebo’s touches this week given his fumbling issue. As usual, the head coach was mum on the plans, but this could be a week when Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr. get bigger roles in the rushing attack to see if they can jumpstart it. On the defensive side, the Giants’ pass rush has finally awakened after a slow start, recording seven sacks over the last two weeks. This week, they face a Saints offensive line that has surrendered three sacks to quarterback Tyler Shough over that same period. Combine that with the opportunistic Giants secondary, which has forced eight turnovers this season , against a Saints offense that has committed 13 giveaways, and the Giants’ quest to remain undefeated at home could get a lot easier. Why the Giants Won’t Beat the Saints Oct 5, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (41) scores a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half at Caesars Superdome. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. Last week in the tie against Washington, it was clearly the latter, having surrendered a season-high 202 yards on the ground. The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. Last week in the tie against Washington, it was clearly the latter, having surrendered a season-high 202 yards on the ground. There are many reasons for the Giants’ struggles in run defense, but one glaring issue has been facing pre-snap motion. Motion changes the look for the defense and has sometimes left players out of position or forced them into bad angles as they try to stop the play from gaining a lot of yards. Under head coach Kellen Moore, the Saints have deployed pre-snap motion on 64% of their offensive snaps this season, the ninth-highest rate in the league, and have a 46% success rate overall when using motion. While they use pre-snap motion more in the passing game, they have used it at a 35% rate in the rushing game. If the Giants, who have allowed opponents 5.2 yards per rush attempt on first down, can’t tighten that up, the Saints will have options on subsequent downs, giving New Orleans an advantage. The other thing that could spoil the Giants’ quest to win their fourth straight game at home is their own aggressiveness on defense. If the Giants, who over the last two weeks have blitzed on 57.8% of opposing quarterbacks’ drop backs, come at the Saints with a similar rate of pressure, they’d better hope that Saints signal-caller Tyler Shough, who per PFF data, has a 102.7 passer rating when throwing the ball in 2.5 seconds or less, doesn’t connect with receivers Chris Olave and Rashid Shaheed for the big pass plays downfield. If I live to be 100 (fingers crossed), I will never understand how the oddsmakers come up with their weekly point spreads. What I do understand is that Harbaugh has this team dialed in, and this matchup against the Saints is overall favorable for the Giants if they play a relatively clean game and keep the ball-security issues out of the mix. The Giants have a lot more going for them at this point in the season than the Saints, including far too many advantages that, if they hit on all cylinders, will get the job done. Following a frustrating 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the Saints (1-4) have dropped three consecutive games, raising questions about the team's direction under second-year head coach Kellen Moore. The struggles have even drawn the attention of team owner Gayle Benson , who recently expressed frustration with the organization's performance and made it clear that continued losing would not be tolerated without consequences. With expectations rising and patience wearing thin, New Orleans faces another difficult challenge against a surprising Giants team that has emerged as an early contender in the NFC East. Here are our predictions for Sunday's game. Grant Chachere, Staff Writer: L 24-17 This is the Saints' first road game since Week 2, and it’s a strategic one at that, as the Saints will immediately fly out of New York for their game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris next week. However, this is a critical game for coach Kellen Moore , and maybe even longtime general manager Mickey Loomis . I don’t think Tyler Shough will have many games like he did last week in the loss to the Vikings, but he will have another matchup against a top-10 defense as the Giants are ninth in total defense. The strength of the defense is its ability to defend the pass, allowing only 199.7 yards per contest, which is good for seventh in the NFL, and have forced six interceptions, which is good for fourth. While I think Shough will do much better, the Giants have the players needed to at least limit Shough, and New Orleans’ rushing attack is one of the NFL’s worst and will be ineffective. While the Giants have struggled to stop the run, they will have no trouble stopping the Saints. At the half, join us for Halftime Studs & Duds . Then, a fter the game, join us for our Biggest Winners & Biggest Losers , our View of the Game , and the Most Important Quotes from Kellen Moore & Players . Defensively, I think the Saints will do enough to keep the game close but not enough to win. The Giants aren’t the greatest offense in the world, but Cam Skattebo is a decent running back, while the receiving threats of Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are going to give the Saints’ defense a heap of trouble. I predict a one-score game in the Meadowlands with the Giants pulling it out. Prediction: Giants 24, Saints 17 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 21-17 Which Saints club will show in the Meadowlands today? Will it be the one from the first three weeks of the season, or the one from the last three? We know this: those leading this organization have been put on notice by the woman that holds the checkbook. For the first time as owner of the Saints, Gayle Benson is faced with a situation that will require resolve and a possible move that will force her to make decisions that will be uncomfortable. She has put her trust and belief in those in charge. After seeing where her club has gone in the last few weeks, and the fan reaction to that direction, Mrs. Benson is having to rethink that trust. Meanwhile, a two-week road trip followed by the Saints open/bye week may be just what the doctor ordered for Moore and his troops: a chance to regroup and rethink where things are. Being a "glass-half-full" kinda guy, I'm getting this feeling this may be the first step to Moore, his coaches, and his players turning things around. However, don't bet the house on who I choose to win today. I've only been right once in five prognostications this year. Stuckey Sun, October 18, 2026 at 3:54 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New Orleans Saints (1-4) and New York Giants (3-1-1) will square off in Week 6 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Saints are 1.5-point favorites over the Giants on the spread, with the over/under set at 45.5 total points. New Orleans is a -115 moneyline favorite to win outright, while New York is listed as a -105 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Saints vs Giants predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, October 18. Saints vs Giants pick: Saints -1.5 (+100) My Giants vs. Saints best bet is New Orleans to cover the spread (-1.5), with the best price currently available at FanDuel . Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Download the Action Network app now for more NFL picks and analysis! Saints vs Giants Odds for NFL Week 6 Saints vs Giants spread: Saints -1.5, Giants +1.5 Saints vs Giants total: over/under 45.5 Saints vs Giants moneyline: Saints -115, Giants -105 New Orleans Saints vs New York Giants Preview The Saints originally opened as underdogs for this game, but almost immediately swung to 1.5-point road favorites — and I think they are sitting at the absolute bottom of their market value. Am I thrilled to back New Orleans on the road here? Not exactly. But I am itching to fade the Giants . Sure, the Saints' run defense is abysmal, but they are facing a Giants team entirely incapable of exploiting it. New Orleans has played a grueling schedule the last two weeks, facing the Falcons (who ran wild with Bijan Robinson) and the Vikings (who have one of the best defenses in the NFL). Offensively, Tyler Shough has been very good when kept clean in the pocket. With the Giants missing Brian Burns , Shough should have all day to operate and consistently move the ball through the air in this game. The Giants are a couple games above .500, but they are arguably the most fraudulent team in the NFL. They could easily be 1-4 right now after lucking out with a tie against the Commanders last week. New York's back-to-back home wins came against the Titans and Cardinals — two incompetent teams that turned the ball over at the goal line with a chance to win. Offensively, the Giants have completely stalled since losing Jaxson Dart. They rank 29th in both rush success rate and rush EPA, meaning their ground game has almost totally vanished. Jameis Winston has thrown for 694 yards with a 6:3 TD:INT ratio in the three games he's started. He's done a good job of feeding Malik Nabers as the Giants' WR1 has surpassed 100 receiving yards in each of the last two weeks. Of course, the thing with Winston is that he's prone to making critical mistakes when throwing into zone coverage. Saints vs Giants Pick, Betting Analysis There is a massive strength-of-schedule disparity here, with the Giants feasting on the easiest schedule in the league so far while the Saints have been heavily battle tested against some of the NFL's best. Without Jaxson Dart's mobility, the Giants simply haven't bee able to run the ball with Cam Skattebo, forcing Jameis Winston into high-variance, mistake-prone dropbacks. The Saints should be able to keep the pocket clean for Tyler Shough throughout this game, which will likely allow him to dissect the Giants' defense and lift his team to a road win. away.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season We just got here. Good travel, all that. Our guys were able to get out on the field and walk around and get a light lift in at the hotel. Obviously, there's a little bit of an acclimation process, but I think it's a great setup. It's an awesome opportunity for our football team to spend some time together while focusing on a really good opportunity to play out here in a great atmosphere. It's been a really fun week. Essentially, it was game, back to the hotel in New York - in New Jersey, technically - and then we flew out. The medical evaluations coming out of the game, you obviously have more time to go through that process. I think this is an important part, getting out here. It's not a perfect setup with the travel and all that sort of stuff. But for us to be able to do it coming right out of the game, get here, now our guys get to get acclimated. They'll get adjusted to this time zone pretty well. We'll get the different place, tourist thing out of our system here quickly and then get into a full week. I thought that was a good first start for him as far as getting out there and playing some football. away.blurb: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Hurts reportedly out for season Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? We're breaking down the final New Orleans Saints injury report for Week 6's road game against the New York Giants . Who's in, who's out, and who has a chance to play? The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? home.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season We just got here. Good travel, all that. Our guys were able to get out on the field and walk around and get a light lift in at the hotel. Obviously, there's a little bit of an acclimation process, but I think it's a great setup. It's an awesome opportunity for our football team to spend some time together while focusing on a really good opportunity to play out here in a great atmosphere. It's been a really fun week. Essentially, it was game, back to the hotel in New York - in New Jersey, technically - and then we flew out. The medical evaluations coming out of the game, you obviously have more time to go through that process. I think this is an important part, getting out here. It's not a perfect setup with the travel and all that sort of stuff. But for us to be able to do it coming right out of the game, get here, now our guys get to get acclimated. They'll get adjusted to this time zone pretty well. We'll get the different place, tourist thing out of our system here quickly and then get into a full week. I thought that was a good first start for him as far as getting out there and playing some football. We were able to score right before half, and then the third quarter, I felt like we came out playing the way we needed to play. home.blurb: Saints Injury Report: Olave Questionable as Giants Face Offensive Line Concerns Skip to main content SI.COM The Saints' top receiving target, Chris Olave , who missed the last two practices with an illness, was a limited participant Friday. If Olave can play Sunday, starting quarterback Tyler Shough can breathe a sigh of relief. On defense, linebacker Kaden Elliss and edge rusher Anfernee Jennings are out again for Sunday. As for the Giants, edge rusher Abdul Carter and starting offensive tackles Jermaine Eluemunor and Andrew Thomas have been listed as questionable. LB Anfernee Jennings: Out (knee) RB Alvin Kamara: Questionable (back) WR Chris Olave: Questionable (illness) DT Nathan Shepherd: Questionable (illness) CB Lorenzo Styles: Questionable (knee) LS Zach Wood: Questionable (calf) LB Abdul Carter: Questionable (calf) T Andrew Thomas: Questionable (groin) T Jermaine Eluemunor: Questionable (calf) CB Colton Hood: Out (concussion) As pressure mounts around the organization , the New Orleans Saints look to end their losing skid and get back on track on the road against the New York Giants on Sunday, but concerns linger over their latest injury report. Olave has recorded 39 catches for 537 yards with a touchdown. Olave is second in the league in receiving yards and is tied for third in receptions. Elliss, who is arguably the Saints’ best player at his position, has been greatly missed as the Saints have allowed 179 yards per game on the ground since his injury during their 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3. Concerns about Season Reach the Top After Saints owner Gayle Benson said the Saints’ 1-4 start was “unacceptable” earlier in the week, head coach Kellen Moore said after practice he speaks with her regularly and communicated with her throughout the week. "We're all just trying to reach the same goal," Moore said. "We all want to win football games, and so we're all working toward that." The availability of both Eluemunor and Thomas could have major implications for Sunday's matchup, particularly against a solid edge rusher rotation of New Orleans’ Carl Granderson , Chase Young and Cameron Jordan . LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team?
